item.title: These swing voters regret voting for Trump and it's influencing their midterm choices
item.description:
Over 180,000 Georgians cast their ballots on the first day of early voting on Tuesday, setting a record for midterm elections. Tuesday's total eclipsed the first day of early voting in 2022 by more than 55,000 votes, state election officials say. Georgia's early voting schedule runs through Oct. 30. "This record-breaking turnout proves that voters have confidence in the integrity of our elections," Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said in a statement. "It’s a testament to our strong election system overseen by 159 of the best county election officials in the country." Georgia's contentious U.S. Senate race erupted into a heated confrontation Tuesday night as Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., accused GOP challenger Rep. item.title: Photos: China and North Korea open new border bridge amid deepening ties
item.description:
China and North Korea opened their biggest land crossing, a sign of closer bilateral ties that are likely to unsettle regional countries. The 3 km (1.9 mile) Yalu River Bridge was first proposed more than 12 years ago, though it was delayed after ties between Beijing and Pyongyang turned frosty . Relations have improved in recent years thanks in large part to China’s strategic competition with the US, and as Beijing looks to manage Pyongyang’s growing ties to Moscow. The reset in relations has led China to ease demands on North Korea to denuclearize, raising fears across the region. “ The implications for the United States and its allies are stark, ” the Sydney-based Lowy Institute wrote. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: Trump Says the Border Is Secure. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott Keeps Declaring an Emergency.
item.description:
Emily Scherer for ProPublica and The Texas Tribune. Source images: The Texas Tribune and documents obtained by ProPublica. Last month, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott repeated a claim he’s made for the past five years. He stated that the number of people crossing the Texas-Mexico border illegally “posed an ongoing and imminent threat” across the state. In doing so, he renewed a border security disaster proclamation that has greatly expanded his powers without going through the state Legislature. item.title: Indian woman and boyfriend get death sentence in 'blue drum' murder case
item.description:
You would have to be living under a rock to be unaware of the Cornell seven case. In short, a Jane Doe has accused a group of men of sexually assaulting her while she was impaired by alcohol and ketamine at a frat party two years ago. She recently filed a civil lawsuit against the alleged perpetrators, and the lawsuit instantly became a viral sensation. So much so that national politicians have gotten involved. New York Governor Kathy Hochul (D) has named state Attorney General Letitia James (D) as a special prosecutor to handle the situation. No charges have been brought against any of the men, and the situation continues to be heavily disputed. item.title: Brazil to shorten workweek in win for Lula ahead of runoff
item.description:
Congress approves constitutional amendment that bans six-day workweeks, which could affect up to 30 million Brazil’s congress has approved a constitutional amendment to shorten the working week to a maximum of 40 hours, a move that could affect 30 million workers and that will hand a political victory to the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ahead of the presidential runoff in under two weeks. In an attempt to overturn the first-round lead secured by his opponent, far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula has strongly championed the amendment, which will give some workers an extra day off each week.
